Wrap long legend entries of a plot

wrapLegendLabels.Rd

Applies automatic line wrapping to the legend entries (key labels) of a plot, so that long entries - such as simulation output paths like Organism|PeripheralVenousBlood|Aciclovir|Plasma (Peripheral Venous Blood) - are broken over several lines instead of shrinking the plot panel or being cut off.

The function wraps the labels of all scales that can contribute to the legend and are mapped in the plot: colour/color, fill, shape and linetype.

  • Scales already present on the plot (e.g. scale_colour_osp() or the LLOQ scale_linetype_manual()) keep their palettes, values and guides - only their labels are wrapped. Named labels and label functions are resolved first, so the wrapped text is exactly what would have been displayed.

  • For aesthetics that are mapped but have no scale yet, a scale of the same type as the one the plot would get at build time is added with wrapped labels (scale_colour_osp() / scale_fill_osp() / scale_shape_osp() for ospsuite.plots plots, the ggplot2 defaults otherwise), so the appearance of the plot is unchanged.

Strings without spaces longer than maxWidth (e.g. compound output paths) are split using stringr::str_wrap(width = maxWidth, whitespace_only = FALSE), so that long tokens are broken into smaller chunks.

Combine with legendWidthFromPlotDimensions() to derive maxWidth from the exported plot size, or use the convenience wrapper wrapLegend().

Usage

wrapLegendLabels(plotObject, maxWidth)

Arguments

plotObject

A ggplot object, e.g. created by plotTimeProfile(), or a CombinedPlot object whose main plot is updated.

maxWidth

Maximum number of characters per legend line.

Value

The ggplot object with wrapped legend labels (the input object is not modified).

See also

Other legend helpers: legendWidthFromPlotDimensions(), wrapLegend()

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  time = rep(seq(1, 24), 2),
  concentration = c(dexp(1:24, 0.2), dexp(1:24, 0.1)),
  output = rep(c(
    "Organism|PeripheralVenousBlood|Aciclovir|Plasma (Peripheral Venous Blood)",
    "Organism|PeripheralVenousBlood|Aciclovir|Muscle (Muscle Interstitial)"
  ), each = 24)
)
p <- plotTimeProfile(
  data = df,
  mapping = aes(x = time, y = concentration, color = output)
)
# wrap legend entries at 20 characters per line
pWrapped <- wrapLegendLabels(p, maxWidth = 20)

# wrap at a width derived from the exported plot dimensions
pWrapped <- wrapLegendLabels(
  p,
  maxWidth = legendWidthFromPlotDimensions(p, plotWidth = 8, unit = "cm")
)
